messages:
Ana (sales): Hey team — AcmeHealth POC is failing when they enable JSON mode + function_call. Client sees a JSON parse error: \"Unexpected token \" in the middle of the response. Happened during streaming.
Ana (sales): Log excerpt:
```
stream_event: {"choices": [{"delta": {"tool_call": "{\"name\": \"summarize\", \"arguments\": {\"summary\": \"Start of JSON...\"}}"}, "finish_reason": null}] }
stream_event: {"choices": [{"delta": {"tool_call": "...truncated json}}\"}, "finish_reason": "stop"}] }
error: client parse failure: unexpected end of input
```
Ana (sales): They say it only fails when streaming; non-streaming works but UX worse. Also saw some 429s in the timeline.
deploy-bot: Incoming rate_limit event for acct-acmehealth at 1934567998 - burst_count=327, limit=300 - returning 429s.
Ravi (eng): Can you paste the request payload they send (headers + usage flags)? Are they using function_call: \"auto\" and providing json_schema?
Ana (sales): Request snippet:
```json
{ "model": "rwd-open-13b", "stream": true, "function_call": "auto", "json_schema": { "type": "object", "properties": { "summary": {"type":"string"} }, "required":["summary"] } }
```
Maya (solutions): This looks like two separate failure modes: 1) streaming truncation leaving an unterminated JSON object; 2) 429 mid-stream causing the connection to close before we finish the structured output. Both will produce parse errors client-side.
Jules (infra): Confirmed from infra traces: there was a short spike, client opened ~12 parallel streams with streaming=true, we hit their burst cap. We returned a few 429s and then some streams cut with partial payloads.
Ravi (eng): We also have a known gap where our stream assembler doesn't guarantee object-boundary atomicity for tool_call chunks when schema validation is applied incrementally. Workaround: either disable streaming or buffer until the function_call completes server-side. Short-term we can add a sanitizer that attempts to close unbalanced braces but it's brittle.
Ana (sales): What's the quick configuration I can ask the customer to change so the POC doesn't block the deal? They want streaming for UI.
Maya (solutions): Two immediate actions: ask them to reduce parallel stream windows (recommend <=5) and implement a client fallback: if JSON parse fails on stream close, retry the same request with stream=false. I'll draft a snippet. Also we can temporarily bump their burst cap for 24h.
Jules (infra): I've bumped acct-acmehealth burst cap to 500 for 24h and enabled verbose streaming logs for their tenant. Link to logs: https://internal-logs/redwood/acct-acmehealth/1934567890 (internal).
Ravi (eng): Client-side snippet to detect and fallback:
```js
// on each stream chunk append to buffer
buffer += chunk
try {
  const obj = JSON.parse(buffer)
  handle(obj)
} catch (e) {
  // if stream ended and parse failed, retry as buffered
  if (streamEnded) {
    fetch('/v1/generate', { method: 'POST', body: originalPayloadWithStreamFalse })
      .then(res => res.json()).then(handle)
  }
}
```
Maya (solutions): For the POC message to Acme: \"Please reduce concurrent stream windows to 5, add simple on_stream_error fallback that retries without streaming, and we'll temporarily increase your burst cap to avoid 429s. If you still see parse errors, send us the raw stream capture and we'll sanitize on our side.\"
QA-Leo: Created tracking ticket INF-3421 for a runtime fix to ensure atomicity of tool_call JSON assembly when streaming+schema validation are enabled. Assigned to Ravi.
Ana (sales): Thanks — I sent the instructions and the fallback snippet. I'll keep them on the bumped cap and report back.
Jules (infra): Cap increase applied at 1934568005 (confirmed). Monitoring shows error rate dropping.
Ana (sales): Acme just confirmed: after lowering parallelism + retry fallback + our temporary cap bump they can complete the POC and validate the outputs. They reported one remaining parse that was fixed by the client retry.
Ana (sales): Closing loop on the thread — we should still track INF-3421 for a proper fix. Thanks all! :tada:
